## The claim

At least one ClinVar pathogenic or likely-pathogenic allele of a target-set gene is present in this sample at heterozygous multiplicity, above the error threshold fitted on the calibration set's homozygous-reference side.

**Prediction if true.** Counting the alternate k-mers of every public ClinVar P/LP allele in every target gene returns at least one allele whose count exceeds the fitted minimum-count threshold and whose posterior favours the het class.

**What would refute it.** No ClinVar P/LP allele clears the fitted error threshold, in which case the causal pair, if any, is novel on both sides and no published allele contributes to it.

One of them has a balanced alternate fraction of 0.471 and was also called by both read-derived callers.   -> 0.769
```
  +0.000  neutral 0.40 — The other four sit at alternate fractions of 0.061 to 0.091, about a tenth of a heterozygote, and no caller reported any of them. The fitted error rate of 0.000247 makes any alternate count of two or more improbable under homozygous reference, so the model calls them heterozygous; they are better read as the error model being too tight than as presence.   -> 0.769
suggested confidence 0.77 (1 supporting, 0 refuting, 1 neutral)
```

The weighing is a transparent heuristic for triage, not a calibrated posterior: the strengths are human judgments, and rows drawn from the same underlying data are not independent the way the sum treats them.

**The committed confidence differs from the suggestion by -0.17.** The reasoning below is why.

| 2 | supported | 0.60 | Five ClinVar P/LP alleles of reachable target genes clear the fitted error threshold with three agreeing probes, so the claim's letter is met. Below the heuristic's 0.77 on purpose: only one of the five has an alternate fraction anywhere near a heterozygote (0.471) and only that one was independently called. The other four sit at 0.06-0.09 and are an artefact of an error rate fitted at 0.000247, which makes any alternate count of two improbable under homozygous reference. The claim is supported by one allele, not five, and the limitation is recorded beside it. |
